quotes: in September 2025, Nvidia announced a partnership and investment in Intel to partner on new data center and client platform products. This partnership may result in increased competition and pricing pressure for our products or could prevent us from participating in other opportunities, which could materially adversely impact our business, financial condition and margins.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A (recent developments) and Q3 2026 earnings slides.
growth_thesis.claim: Acquisitions of Taalas Inc. and World Labs Technologies (expected to close Q4 2026) are intended to strengthen AMD's model research, inference capabilities and super-intelligence hardware/software/systems development.
quotes: In August and September 2026, we entered into definitive agreements to acquire Taalas Inc. and World Labs Technologies, Inc. to strengthen our model research and inference capabilities and development of future super intelligence (SI) hardware, software and systems.
Announced agreements to acquire World Labs and Taalas, expanding AMD capabilities across the full superintelligence stack.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A (recent developments) as a description of commercial arrangements.
growth_thesis.claim: AMD's growth strategy involves committing capital to cloud compute capacity and data center leases to support the broader AI infrastructure ecosystem, creating both an opportunity and a financial obligation.
quotes: Under our cloud compute capacity arrangements, we have committed, and expect to continue to commit in the future, to purchase GPU compute capacity from cloud service providers (CSPs) either to the extent it is not successfully placed with third-party customers, or for capacity we reserved and may sell or assign to third parties.

We entered into data center leases which we expect to assign or sublease to commercial partners, and provided credit support to certain commercial partners in the form of guarantees of their lease and debt obligations in the event of their default.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A and Q3 2026 earnings press release; the margin figures are from the unaudited condensed consolidated statements of operations.
growth_thesis.claim: Gross margin expansion (54% GAAP in Q3 2026 vs. 52% a year earlier) is driven by favorable product mix toward higher-margin Data Center revenue, and must continue for profitability to scale with revenue.
quotes: Gross margin for the three months ended September 26, 2026 was 54% compared to gross margin of 52% for the prior year period, a 2 percentage point increase primarily driven by a favorable product mix, including higher Data Center segment revenue.
Gross margin | 54% | 52% | Up 2 ppts | 54% | Flat

material_events.basis: stated in the cited 8-K (Item 1.01) and confirmed in the 10-Q MD&A
material_events.claim: AMD closed a public offering of $4.75 billion aggregate principal amount of senior notes in four tranches (2029, 2031, 2033, 2036).
quotes: On August 17, 2026 (the "Closing Date"), Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (the "Company") closed its public offering (the "Offering") of $4.75 billion aggregate principal amount of senior notes, consisting of $1.25 billion aggregate principal amount of its 4.600% Senior Notes due 2029 (the "2029 Notes"), $1.50 billion aggregate principal amount of its 5.000% Senior Notes due 2031 (the "2031 Notes"), $1.00 billion aggregate principal amount of its 5.250% Senior Notes due 2033 (the "2033 Notes") and $1.00 billion aggregate principal amount of its 5.500% Senior Notes due 2036 (the "2036 Notes"
In August 2026, we issued $4.75 billion in aggregate principal amount of senior notes, with proceeds intended for general corporate purposes, including the repayment of debt.

material_events.claim: AMD repaid in full the $875 million aggregate principal amount of its 4.212% Senior Notes as they matured in September 2026.
quotes: We also repaid in full the $875 million aggregate principal amount of our 4.212% Senior Notes as the notes matured in September 2026.

material_events.claim: AMD entered into definitive agreements to acquire Taalas Inc. and World Labs Technologies, Inc. to strengthen model research, inference capabilities and SI hardware/software/systems development; closings expected in Q4 fiscal 2026 subject to regulatory approvals.
quotes: In August and September 2026, we entered into definitive agreements to acquire Taalas Inc. and World Labs Technologies, Inc. to strengthen our model research and inference capabilities and development of future super intelligence (SI) hardware, software and systems. The acquisitions are expected to close in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026, subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions.

material_events.basis: stated in the 10-K Business section and MD&A
material_events.claim: AMD entered into a product purchase agreement with OpenAI OpCo, LLC to deploy 6 gigawatts of AMD GPUs, with the first gigawatt powered by AMD Instinct MI450 series products; concurrently AMD issued a warrant to purchase up to 160 million shares at $0.01 per share.
quotes: In October 2025, we entered into a product purchase agreement with OpenAI OpCo, LLC, (OpenAI) to deploy 6 gigawatts of AMD GPUs, with the deployment of the first gigawatt of capacity powered by our AMD Instinct MI450 series products.
Concurrent with the agreement, we issued to OpenAI a warrant to purchase up to an aggregate of 160 million shares of AMD's common stock at an exercise price of $0.01 per share.

material_events.basis: stated in the 10-K MD&A and Business section
material_events.claim: AMD completed the acquisition of ZT Systems for $3.2 billion in cash and 8.3 million shares of common stock, retaining the ZT Design Business.
quotes: In March 2025, we completed the acquisition of ZT Systems for $3.2 billion in cash and 8.3 million shares of our common stock.
In March 2025, we acquired ZT Group Int'l, Inc. (ZT Systems), where we retained certain intellectual property and employees associated with the design operations (ZT Design Business).

material_events.basis: stated in the 10-K MD&A and Business section
material_events.claim: AMD sold the ZT data center infrastructure manufacturing business to Sanmina Corporation for $2.4 billion in cash and 1.2 million shares of Sanmina common stock, with contingent consideration of up to $450 million.
quotes: in October 2025, we sold the ZT data center infrastructure manufacturing business (ZT Manufacturing Business) to Sanmina Corporation (Sanmina) for $2.4 billion in cash, subject to certain purchase price adjustments, and 1.2 million shares of Sanmina common stock. We are eligible to receive additional contingent cash consideration of up to $450 million from Sanmina to the extent certain conditions are met.

material_events.claim: AMD recorded approximately $800 million of inventory and related charges on AMD Instinct MI308 Data Center GPU products in Q2 2025 due to new U.S. export restrictions on certain semiconductors to China; approximately $360 million was reversed in Q4 2025 when licensed shipments began.
quotes: During the second quarter of fiscal year 2025, the Company recorded approximately $800 million of inventory and related charges on AMD Instinct MI308 Data Center GPU products due to new U.S. export restrictions on certain semiconductors to China.
During the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025, we began shipping products and reversed approximately $360 million of the inventory and related charges recorded earlier in the year.

material_events.basis: stated in the 8-K (Item 5.02) and accompanying press release
material_events.claim: Director Joe Householder retired from AMD's Board effective August 19, 2026, and Tim Ryan was appointed as a new director effective the same date; KC McClure became chair of the Audit and Finance Committee.
quotes: On August 17, 2026, Mr. Joe Householder provided Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (the "Company") with notice of his intention to retire from the Company's Board of Directors (the "Board") effective as of August 19, 2026.
In connection with Mr. Householder's retirement, on August 19, 2026, the Board appointed Mr. Tim Ryan as a member of the Board effective as of August 19, 2026.

risks.basis: Stated in P3 (OpenAI agreement), P4 and P5 (customer concentration language), and P2 (loss of significant customer risk factor).
risks.claim: AMD's revenue growth is heavily concentrated in a small number of customers, including a 6-gigawatt GPU purchase agreement with OpenAI, creating single-customer dependency that could impair the Data Center growth thesis if demand falters.
quotes: In October 2025, we entered into a product purchase agreement with OpenAI OpCo, LLC, (OpenAI) to deploy 6 gigawatts of AMD GPUs, with the deployment of the first gigawatt of capacity powered by our AMD Instinct MI450 series products.
a small number of customers will continue to account for a substantial part of AMD's revenue and receivables in the future

If one of our key customers decides to stop buying our products, materially reduces its operations or its demand for our products, or has operations that are materially impaired for a significant period of time such that it is unable to receive or utilize our products, or pay its liabilities, our business would be materially adversely affected.

risks.basis: Stated in P2 (Risk Factors) and P5 (10-Q Risk Factors); the specific partnership is named and dated in P2.
risks.claim: The September 2025 Nvidia-Intel partnership on data center and client platform products poses a direct competitive threat to AMD's Data Center GPU and CPU leadership, potentially compressing margins and limiting market share gains.
quotes: in September 2025, Nvidia announced a partnership and investment in Intel to partner on new data center and client platform products

This partnership may result in increased competition and pricing pressure for our products or could prevent us from participating in other opportunities, which could materially adversely impact our business, financial condition and margins.

Nvidia Corporation (Nvidia) leverages its market position in data center GPU, financial resources, and proprietary software ecosystem to promote its systems and influences customers who do business with us.

risks.basis: Stated in P3 (MD&A, specific dollar figures and regulatory context) and P5 (10-Q Risk Factors, general export control risk).
risks.claim: U.S. export controls on AMD Instinct MI308 GPUs to China already generated approximately $440 million in net inventory and related charges in fiscal 2025, and further restrictions could impair revenue and margins on future products.
quotes: approximately $440 million of net inventory and related charges associated with the U.S. government export control on AMD Instinct™ MI308 Data Center GPU products

Government actions and regulations, including export controls, national-security-based regulations, import tariffs and trade protection measures, may limit our ability to export our products to certain customers, increase costs, harm our competitive position and materially affect our business.

U.S. government officials have expressed an expectation that the U.S. government will receive 15% of the revenue generated from licensed MI308 sales to China; however, to date, the U.S. government has not published a regulation establishing such requirement.

a decrease in our Client and Gaming segment revenue primarily due to lower demand for semi-custom products

risks.basis: Stated in P2 and P5 (Risk Factors, cyclical language) and P7 (current growth rate). The inventory figures are from F1 (balance sheet).
risks.claim: The semiconductor industry is highly cyclical and has experienced severe downturns, and AMD's rapid revenue growth (45% YoY in Q3 2026) may be unsustainable if AI infrastructure spending normalizes or a cyclical downturn hits end-market demand.
quotes: The semiconductor industry is highly cyclical and has experienced severe downturns that have materially adversely affected, and may continue to materially adversely affect, our business in the future.

We have incurred substantial losses in previous downturns, due to substantial declines in average selling prices; the cyclical nature of supply and demand imbalances in the semiconductor industry; a decline in demand for end-user products that incorporate our products; and excess inventory levels and periods of inventory adjustment.
the near-term and long-term trajectory of such generative AI solutions is unknown
